stem: A highly sensitized kidney waitlist candidate is due for routine waitlist management testing. According to common center practice described in pre-transplant references, how often should panel reactive antibody (PRA) testing typically be obtained?

options.text: Once every five years regardless of clinical change
Only at the time of transplant surgery

explanation.rationale_correct: For sensitized kidney candidates, references describe monthly or more frequent PRA testing as part of waitlist management and risk monitoring.

rationale_incorrect.B: Sensitized candidates require much more frequent antibody monitoring than every five years.
rationale_incorrect.C: PRA monitoring occurs during the waiting period, not only intraoperatively.
rationale_incorrect.D: Ongoing PRA surveillance continues after listing for sensitized candidates.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: Monthly (or more frequent) PRAs for candidates who are sensitized

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 1 → kidney waitlist management → §7.c.ii (monthly or more frequent PRAs for sensitized candidates); PDF p. 55 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Anchor verified against docs/reference/cupples-core-curriculum-2e.pdf p. 55.

stem: A liver candidate's MELD score changes after updated labs, affecting waitlist priority. What is the coordinator's responsibility regarding this change?

options.text: Educate the candidate about the waitlist status change and rationale for additional testing or procedures
Withhold all waitlist information until the candidate is called in for transplant
Remove the candidate from the list without team discussion
Delegate all waitlist communication to the dialysis unit without transplant team involvement

explanation.rationale_correct: Waitlist management references assign coordinators responsibility to educate candidates about changes in waitlist status and the rationale for additional tests or procedures.

rationale_incorrect.B: Candidates should receive education about waitlist status changes rather than being kept uninformed.
rationale_incorrect.C: Listing changes require interdisciplinary team processes, not unilateral coordinator removal.
rationale_incorrect.D: Transplant coordinators remain responsible for waitlist education even when dialysis centers participate in care.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → §9. Waitlist management → c.i. Transplant coordinator responsibilities → iv.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Educate candidates about any changes in their waitlist status and rationale

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → §9. Waitlist management → coordinator responsibilities → item iv.; PDF p. 102 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Anchor verified against docs/reference/cupples-core-curriculum-2e.pdf p. 102.

stem: During pre-operative coordination for an adult heart transplant, which test is listed among typical preoperative requirements before surgery?

options.text: Routine elective coronary bypass for all candidates

explanation.rationale_correct: Typical preoperative protocols include obtaining a chest radiograph along with laboratory tests and other required studies before transplant surgery.

rationale_incorrect.B: Coronary bypass is not a universal preoperative requirement for every heart candidate.
rationale_incorrect.C: LAS applies to lung allocation, not standard heart preoperative protocols.
rationale_incorrect.D: PELD applies to pediatric liver allocation, not heart preoperative coordination.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 9, Heart Transplantation → Preparation of Patient for Surgery → A.1
